memory_update.text: AMKR should remain a reference anchor for US-listed advanced-packaging capacity and for tracing substrate, inspection, metrology, and bonding-equipment suppliers.
CAMT appears to be one of the cleanest US-listed underfollowed yield-enablement names because public disclosures explicitly mention HBM, chiplets, hybrid bonding, inspection, and 3D measurement.

ONTO belongs in the underfollowed discovery lane as a broader process-control company with specific advanced IC substrate, panel-level packaging, AI/HPC, metrology, lithography, and analytics exposure.
KLIC is a second-order advanced-packaging tooling candidate; its evidence is real but must be tested for durability of AI-related thermocompression bonding demand.

US-listed pure-play substrate and surface-chemistry exposure remains limited. Additional non-US or OTC ADR searches should test Ajinomoto/ABF film, MEC surface chemistry, Ibiden, Shinko, Kinsus, Unimicron, and AT&S, but those were not included here unless US-listing/liquidity can be confirmed.

MKSI should be tracked as a US-listed surface-chemistry and substrate-process candidate through Atotech, especially for FC-BGA, package-substrate plating, adhesion promotion, laser drilling, and wet-processing exposure.
CAMT has direct evidence of AI/HBM advanced-packaging inspection and metrology exposure through announced Hawk orders and product positioning.
FORM maps to HBM and advanced-packaging yield enablement through known-good-die, probe-card, and wafer-level test requirements; treat as indirect but plausible bottleneck exposure.

For US-listed names, the substrate-maker layer itself is sparse; better mappings are adjacent chokepoints: surface chemistry/equipment, inspection/metrology, wafer/package test, and OSAT 2.5D capacity.

Non-US-listed or OTC Asia/Europe substrate and material names such as Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, Ajinomoto, and MEC may be more direct to the node but require a separate non-US-listed pass.

CAMT is the strongest US-listed underfollowed discovery candidate for the HBM/AI advanced-packaging yield-enablement lane because official materials map directly to advanced packaging and gathered evidence references orders from a leading HBM manufacturer.

AMKR should be retained as a US-listed reference anchor for advanced packaging capacity, but not treated as the primary underfollowed discovery name because its market cap and attention level are higher.

ENTG maps to the surface-chemistry/materials-handling side of the node, but AI/HBM-specific revenue linkage is currently an inference that must be verified through filings, management commentary, or customer qualification evidence.

Many of the purest substrate and surface-chemistry suppliers cited in the node thesis are not straightforward US-listed small/mid-cap names; later layers should search ADR/OTC availability, Asia listings, customer concentration, liquidity, and governance risk.

COHU remains a speculative shadow candidate until evidence proves exposure to HBM, AI accelerator packages, advanced OSAT customers, or package-level inspection/test bottlenecks rather than broad cyclical semiconductor test demand.

The most direct substrate and surface-chemistry chokepoints in this node appear to be non-US-listed or not cleanly US-listed: Ajinomoto for ABF-like insulating film, MEC Company for copper-bonding surface chemistry, and Asian substrate makers including Ibiden, Unimicron, Kinsus, AT&S, and Shinko. US-listed discovery should therefore emphasize OSAT, inspection/metrology, and package-test pull-through unless ADR/OTC eligibility is allowed in a separate pass.
AMKR is a plausible US-listed second-order AI advanced-packaging capacity candidate, but it needs customer and revenue-mix verification to separate AI/HBM pull-through from broad OSAT cyclicality.

CAMT is a stronger underfollowed yield-enablement candidate because public company materials explicitly reference advanced packaging and large orders tied to a tier-1 OSAT and a leading HBM manufacturer.
FORM is a low-attention HBM/advanced-packaging test candidate; the key next filter is whether HBM probe-card demand is material enough to change company-level revenue and margins.

node: HBM and AI accelerator advanced-packaging substrate and surface-chemistry layer
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the advanced-packaging substrate, bonding, inspection, and yield-enablement layer beneath obvious HBM producers and AI accelerator leaders. The cleanest direct exposure appears to sit in specialty inspection/metrology, bonding equipment, OSAT advanced-packaging platforms, and ABF-like substrate materials rather than in GPU or memory producers themselves. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the US-listed universe one layer beneath obvious HBM producers and GPU leaders. The direct US-listed substrate-maker universe appears thin, so the cleaner US-listed mappings are advanced-packaging OSAT capacity, surface-treatment and plating chemistry/equipment, inspection/metrology, and wafer/package test yield-enablement. Reference leaders remain useful as demand anchors, but the underfollowed lane is concentrated in MKSI, CAMT, FORM, and AMKR rather than memory producers or mega-cap foundries. Layer 1B expanded the US-listed universe around the HBM/AI-accelerator advanced-packaging substrate, chemistry, inspection, and yield-enablement layer. The cleanest direct public-market exposure is still limited because many key substrate and chemistry suppliers are Asia-listed or embedded inside larger materials companies. For US-listed names, the best two-lane map is: Amkor as the outsourced advanced-packaging reference anchor, Camtek as a higher-purity inspection/metrology discovery candidate with explicit HBM order signals, Entegris as a larger materials/contamination-control candidate tied to advanced packaging
